name: security-react-native-js-native-authority-review
intent: React Native JavaScript-to-native module capability boundaries
artifacts: Native module methods, JS bundle/content trust, argument validation and platform permission/caller context.
trace: Determine whether lower-trust JS/content can reach privileged native methods and choose resources/actions beyond its authorized feature.
experiment: Use an owned app fixture with an inert native operation and synthetic JS input; compare intended calls and a forbidden resource selection.
disproof: A powerful native module exposed to fully trusted application JS is not itself a defect; establish a lower-trust caller path.
repair: Constrain module arguments and capabilities at the native boundary and retest intended application use.
branch_decisions: Define whether JavaScript is trusted bundled code or lower-trust remotely supplied content. A native method exposed to the trusted application runtime is not automatically a web-origin bridge. Trace the actual entry from WebView/messages/updates into module arguments, native permissions and object checks before claiming another origin can invoke it.
operational_method: Resolve legacy bridge versus New Architecture/TurboModule registration, the actual exported native method and per-platform argument conversion. Find the lower-trust entry into that method before treating bundled application JS as an attacker. Compare a legitimate native invocation with a malformed/foreign-resource value at the real conversion boundary using an owned app fixture; a generic mock bridge cannot prove installed module exposure.
